original_question: Fix integers k > 3 and Delta > 3. For all but finitely many connected graphs G of maximum degree Delta, is the list-chromatic number of the k-th power bounded by chi_l(G^k) <= sum_{i=1}^k Delta (Delta - 1)^(i-1) + 1 - k, and does the same bound also hold for the painting number chi_p(G^k)?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 15 in Section 6, which asks for the list-coloring and painting analogues of the higher-power coloring bound proved in Theorem 43; the needed notation and motivation come from Section 5.3. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper's intended problem: it fixes k and Δ, uses the 'all but finitely many connected graphs' quantifier, restricts to graphs with maximum degree Δ, gives the exact bound D_{k,Δ}+1-k in expanded form, and asks for both the list-chromatic and painting versions. Also, your notation χℓ(G^k) and χp(G^k) is mathematically equivalent in content to the paper's superscript-k notation. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
missing_details: The paper's parameter range is k ≥ 3 and Δ ≥ 3, not k > 3 and Δ > 3; your draft unintentionally excludes the boundary cases k = 3 and Δ = 3 that are part of the stated problem. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

To be fully stand-alone, the k-th power G^k should be defined as the graph on V(G) in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when their distance in G is at most k. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

The bound is naturally written using D_{k,Δ}, which Section 5.3 defines as the largest possible degree of a vertex in the k-th power of a graph of maximum degree Δ, with D_{k,Δ} = Σ_{i=1}^k Δ(Δ-1)^(i-1) = Δ((Δ-1)^k-1)/(Δ-2). ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

For a fully self-contained statement, χp should be identified as the paint number (online list chromatic number), defined via the k-painting game. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

The fixed-parameter quantifier structure should be explicit: for each fixed pair (k, Δ), there are only finitely many exceptional connected graphs with maximum degree Δ. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

The paper presents this as an open problem/question, not as a theorem or established equivalence; Theorem 43 is only the ordinary coloring analogue. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
refined_question: Fix integers k ≥ 3 and Δ ≥ 3, and let D_{k,Δ} := Σ_{i=1}^k Δ(Δ-1)^(i-1) = Δ((Δ-1)^k-1)/(Δ-2), the largest possible degree of a vertex in the k-th power of a graph of maximum degree Δ. If G^k denotes the graph obtained from a connected graph G by joining every pair of vertices whose distance in G is at most k, then for all but finitely many connected graphs G with Δ(G) = Δ, must one have χℓ(G^k) ≤ D_{k,Δ} + 1 - k, and likewise χp(G^k) ≤ D_{k,Δ} + 1 - k, where χp is the paint number (online list chromatic number)? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the higher-powers problem rather than any square-coloring or planar subsection: the exact quantity Σ_{i=1}^k Δ(Δ-1)^(i-1)+1-k appears in Section 5.3 as D_{k,Δ}+1-k, Theorem 43 proves that bound for ordinary coloring, and Open Problem 15 in Section 6 asks for precisely the list-coloring and painting analogues. The only substantive corrections needed are the endpoint conditions k ≥ 3 and Δ ≥ 3, plus making the definitions of G^k, D_{k,Δ}, and χp explicit so the question is fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
